implemented: bounded fast/slow EWMA service-time estimation for nonstationary load
per-workload p95 latency, class-inflight, batch-size, and minimum-evidence budgets
bounded adaptive safety factor from fast/slow divergence and service-time deviation
hard refusal for unknown classes, insufficient evidence, invalid state, global capacity, class capacity, batch limits, and p95 budget breach
legacy fixed admission APIs preserved without semantic replacement
adversarial_proof: sudden latency shock raises change ratio and safety factor then flips admission to refusal
one workload class cannot borrow evidence from another
interactive and bulk classes can reach different decisions under the same total queue state
capacity and batch caps remain hard refusals regardless of learned estimate
unknown classes and invalid load snapshots fail closed
truth_boundaries: service-time observations are caller supplied and are not authenticated provider telemetry
the estimator is bounded deterministic EWMA adaptation, not arbitrary online policy learning
model evidence does not yet expire by freshness or survive process restart
budget state is local to one controller instance and is not distributed or quorum coordinated
no Groq affiliation, adoption, production deployment, or internal scheduler knowledge is claimed
